name: datapass-vscode

datapass.diagramCloud.url.description: Where DiagramCloud runs (https://…, or http://localhost for a dev server). Opened by "Open Architecture in DiagramCloud"; no project data is ever put in the URL.

datapass.mongoku.url.description: Where your Mongoku runs (https://…, or http://localhost:3100 for a local server). Used for "Open in Mongoku"; DataPass appends only ?project=<entity id>. No credentials.

datapass.foil.controlRoot.description: Local path to foil-control-v1. Leave blank for workspace auto-detection.

datapass.foil.databricksRoot.description: Local path to foil_databrick_dab. Leave blank for workspace auto-detection.

datapass.foil.oracleSshHost.description: SSH config host alias for the FOIL Oracle VM. Do not put credentials here.

datapass.fabric.toolboxRoot.description: Optional local clone of microsoft/fabric-toolbox or fabric-toolbox_J.

datapass.grafana.generatorCommand.description: Dashboard generator command used by gcx dev serve, for example: npm run generate:grafana.

datapass.grafana.watchPath.description: Optional path passed to gcx dev serve --watch.

datapass.catalogs.description: Absolute paths of DataPass project catalogs (datapass.catalog JSON, e.g. <hub clone>/.datapass/catalog.json) listed by "Switch Project". A catalog lists projects and their coordination repositories; no credentials.

datapass.projectsFolders.description: Absolute folders where you keep clones (e.g. D:\PROJ). DataPass looks there, besides the project folder's parent, for the repositories a project declares, and checks each clone's Git origin.

datapass.powerOps.path.description: Absolute path of the Power Ops program (JUtilityPalette.exe) started by "Open Power Ops". Machine-level user setting: a workspace can never choose which program DataPass starts. Nothing is passed to it.

datapass.layout.showInSecondarySideBar.description: The first time a DataPass project opens in a workspace, show DataPass (AI exchange and Details) in the secondary side bar instead of VS Code's Chat. VS Code then remembers the tab you use there; Chat stays one click away at the top of that side bar.

datapass.company.markdownDescription: Company this window stands for (FOIL, DataPass, a client), shown in the status-bar switcher. Set in the company's `.code-workspace` file by *DataPass: Create the Company Workspace File*. Empty: the project's title.

datapass.startupView.markdownDescription: Work view DataPass applies when this workspace opens (the id or name of a view saved in `.datapass/local/views.json`). Read only from a `.code-workspace` file, never from a folder's settings. Work views are saved per computer.

datapass.git.ghPath.description: Absolute path of the GitHub CLI (gh) the Git view uses to list pull requests and their CI; empty = gh from PATH. A .js file runs with VS Code's own Node (a wrapper or a test stub). Machine-level user setting: a workspace can never choose which program DataPass runs. Only `gh auth status` and `gh pr list` are run; the token is never read.

datapass.git.showOtherRepositories.description: Show an "Other repositories" section in the Git view: the Git repositories directly under datapass.projectsFolders (at most 60), read only when you open the section.

datapass.ai.workOrders.enabled.markdownDescription: **Work orders** (0.20): let DataPass prepare orders for Claude Code or Codex and hand them to the desktop apps or a terminal. They use your Claude or Codex plan. Machine-level user setting: a cloned repository can never switch this on. A project can still switch them off (`modules.workOrders: false`), and a **work** project needs `modules.workOrders: true`.

datapass.ai.projectTypes.markdownDescription: Project types on this computer, by project id (`{"foil-v1": "work"}`). Wins over `project.type` in the project's manifest. **dev** and **perso**: work orders on, the agent merges its PRs when CI is green. **work** (FOIL, clients): work orders off unless the project turns them on, and you merge.

enumDescriptions: Claude desktop app: DataPass copies the prompt and opens the app
Claude Code CLI in a VS Code terminal (exact session id)
ChatGPT desktop app (Codex): DataPass copies the prompt and opens the app
Codex CLI in a VS Code terminal (when installed)
datapass.ai.defaultTool.description: Where a new work order goes by default.

datapass.ai.defaultEffort.description: Default effort of a new work order.

datapass.ai.defaultModel.description: Default model of a new work order (letters, digits, dots and dashes); empty = your tool's own default.

datapass.ai.branchPrefix.description: Planned branch of a work order: this prefix plus the order id (dp/wo-20260925-1830-k3f9).

datapass.ai.terminalLocation.description: Where a terminal launch opens: a tab in the editor area (the diagram below, the AI view on the right) or the panel.

datapass.ai.exportScope.description: What 'Attach an export JSON' and 'Export JSON…' cover: the whole project, the selected sub-project, or the company (every DataPass project of this window).

datapass.ai.claude.path.description: Absolute path of the Claude Code CLI for terminal launches; empty = claude from an absolute PATH entry. A .js file runs with VS Code's own Node (a wrapper or a test stub). Machine-level: a workspace can never choose which program runs.

datapass.ai.codex.path.description: Absolute path of the Codex CLI for terminal launches; empty = codex from an absolute PATH entry. Machine-level.

datapass.ai.workLog.privateRepository.markdownDescription: Absolute folder of a **private** Git clone that collects every project's work-order summary (`work-logs/<project id>.json`) when you *Publish summary*. Never this public repository or a repository of the project; on GitHub, `gh` must say it is private (else DataPass asks). DataPass writes the file; you commit and push.

datapass.ai.quickLinks.markdownDescription: Links at the top of the **Claude & Codex** panel (0.24). Only `https:` pages, `claude:` links (the Claude app) and `http://` on 127.0.0.1 or localhost open; others are left out with a note. Yours, never the project's.

datapass.control.enabled.markdownDescription: Read **Claude Control** (your local dashboard) for the Claude & Codex panel and the Work orders view: conversation status, tokens, plan usage, *À faire par toi*. Off = DataPass sends no request to Control at all. Nothing is ever sent to Control; DataPass only reads.

datapass.control.url.description: Claude Control's address. Loopback only (http://127.0.0.1:<port> or http://localhost:<port>); any other address is refused. Machine-level: a workspace can never point DataPass elsewhere.

datapass.control.folder.description: Absolute folder of your claude-control repository, used only to build the start command DataPass copies when Control is off (python server/server.py). DataPass never starts Control itself.

datapass.checks.onSave.description: Check JSON, YAML, databricks.yml, Dockerfiles and compose files when they are saved. Parse-only: nothing is ever run.

datapass.checks.maxFiles.description: Files a repository check looks at before it stops and reports itself incomplete.

datapass.checks.maxFileBytes.description: Files larger than this (bytes) are skipped by the format checks, never read.

enumDescriptions: Native Explorer, DataPass's Git view and the AI exchange (guided tab). Third-party extensions are untouched.
Vanilla plus the architecture diagram (opened with the project) and Details.
Standard plus the Project tree, options, project sheet, readiness, the Agent and Manual tabs.
Everything, as in 0.20 (board, Work and Galaxy views, tool-health status item).
datapass.experience.preset.markdownDescription: DataPass mode: which DataPass views, tabs and sections are shown. Modes change presentation only: the same project files in every mode, commands stay in the Command Palette, and safety blockers always show. Switch with **DataPass: Switch Mode** (status bar).

view.project.description: Project tree: Sub-projects, components, repositories and readiness (left side bar)

view.git.description: Git view: Repositories, worktrees, pull requests with CI, Needs you

view.work.description: Work view: Module cards and capability operations (V2)

view.galaxy.description: Galaxy view: Platform cards and qualification (V1)

view.architecture.description: Architecture panel: The project diagram (bottom panel)

view.aiExchange.description: AI view: Copy a DataPass file for your AI, paste its answer (secondary side bar)

view.details.description: Details: The selected component or sub-project (secondary side bar)

ai.agent.description: AI view: Agent tab: Work orders for Claude Code or Codex (still opt-in per machine and project type)

ai.manual.description: AI view: Manual tab: Where things stand and the route to each official tool

project.subprojects.description: Project tree: sub-projects and components: The architecture as a tree

project.repositories.description: Project tree: Repositories: Cloned, not cloned, planned; commits to get

project.options.description: Project tree: Architecture options: Decisions and scenarios from options.json

project.sheet.description: Project tree: Project sheet: Datasets, formulas, runtimes

project.board.description: Project tree: Board: Tasks, bugs and sprints from board.json

project.readiness.description: Project tree: Readiness and local environment: Full sections (blockers show in every mode)

project.problems.description: Project tree: Problems in project files: What DataPass found wrong in .datapass files

workbench.options.description: Workbench: Options: Compare scenarios, preview, record a decision

workbench.sheet.description: Workbench: Project sheet: The project sheet as tables

workbench.workOrders.description: Workbench: Work orders: Orders handed to Claude Code or Codex

status.mode.description: Status bar: DataPass mode: Shows the mode; click to switch

status.health.description: Status bar: tool health: Tools and bindings ready (opens the Galaxy view)

landing.architecture.description: Open on the architecture: Focus the Architecture panel when a project opens (a workspace's startup view wins)

badge.alternatives.description: "Alternatives exist" on components: Marks components an options.json decision can change

project.variantFilter.description: Project tree: selected architecture and All variants: The tree follows the previewed scenario; a toggle lists every option's components and files

badge.codingState.description: Coding state of options and scenarios: coded / partly coded / not coded, derived from the files DataPass finds

workbench.toolkit.description: Workbench: Toolkit: Tools with their free tier and prices, recipes, what needs a newer DataPass

project.toolkit.description: Project tree: Toolkit: Hub toolkit files read, entries skipped, Needs a newer DataPass

badge.hubChanged.description: "Changed by the hub" on catalogue entries: Marks built-in tools a hub toolkit file changed

view.agentPanel.description: Claude & Codex panel: Quick links, Claude Control status, plan usage, this project's conversations and your to-dos (secondary side bar)

datapass.experience.overrides.markdownDescription: Your changes to the mode: surface id → `true` (show) or `false` (hide). Kept when you switch mode. Easier with **DataPass: Customize DataPass Mode**.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Open the folder (or repository) that holds your project's .datapass/project.json.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
[Switch Project…](command:datapass.switchProject)
[How to prepare a project](command:datapass.openPreparationGuide)

Open a folder to plan and prepare DataPass work.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

Open a folder to see its repositories, worktrees and pull requests.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

scripts.verify: npm run check && npm test && npm run build

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode DataPass reads the project files but never runs Git or other programs inside the workspace: repository state is shown as not inspected, and Check for updates, Get updates, cloning and command operations are disabled until you trust the folder.
